chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Hamzah, he raised it (to the Imam) and said:
Do not eat the meat of a lamb that suckled from the milk of a sow.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: All these narrations are to be understood as referring to the case where it suckled from the sow a complete suckling period, so its meat and blood grew and its strength became firm because of that. But if it was a single suckling or two sucklings, or something that does not cause the meat to grow and the bone to strengthen, then there is no harm in eating its meat after its purification, as we will mention, God willing.

And he explicitly mentioned that in the first hadith when the questioner asked him, so he said: 'It suckled from a sow until it grew up and its bone became firm,' so he answered him at that time with what we mentioned, and that which indicates that.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat the meat of a lamb that drank milk from a pig?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Al-Istibsar*, highlighting the juristic distinction made by Imam al-Hasan (or the narrator) between complete and incomplete suckling. The prohibition applies only when the suckling is sufficient to transform the animal's flesh and blood, whereas brief nursing does not render the meat impure, provided the animal undergoes the prescribed period of purification (*istibra*).
